questions.stem: Let f(z) = z^3 + 2z^2 - 3z + 1 and g(z) = z^2 + 4. Use Rouché's theorem to determine how many zeros of the function f(z) - g(z) are inside the circle |z| = 2.

questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to directly compare f(z) with g(z) instead of considering their difference h(z). Rouché's theorem requires comparing the magnitudes of f(z) - g(z) on the boundary, not just f and g individually. This would lead to an incorrect conclusion about the number of zeros inside the circle.
